subject.title: [Bug]: WhatsApp quoted reply can reach the agent without quoted context

question: When a WhatsApp reply supplies an identifier but omits its quoted body, should OpenClaw show only a structural unavailable-reference by default, or may it recover cached body text under defined safe conditions?
rationale: This is a user-visible context-recovery choice with a privacy boundary: an omitted body can mean transport loss, but may also mean the source intentionally did not provide the message content.

options.title: Default to structural context
options.body: Preserve a trustworthy reply identifier and clearly mark the quoted body unavailable; recover text only after a narrowly specified safe-source contract is established.

options.title: Allow bounded cache recovery
options.body: Use the existing TTL cache when the available Baileys fields prove the quote is ordinary recoverable content, with explicit tests for unavailable-content exclusions.

options.title: Keep current omission
options.body: Continue dropping reply context unless WhatsApp supplies the body, avoiding any risk of re-exposing withheld content at the cost of ambiguous agent prompts.

recommendation.title: Default to structural context
recommendation.body: Preserve a trustworthy reply identifier and clearly mark the quoted body unavailable; recover text only after a narrowly specified safe-source contract is established.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged quote-metadata work is the strongest available current-main history connection to the relevant cache contract.
